source.text: Ὁ δὲ Σαῦλος ἔτι ἐμπνέων ἀπειλῆς καὶ φόνου εἰς τοὺς μαθητὰς τοῦ κυρίου, προσελθὼν τῷ ἀρχιερεῖ ᾐτήσατο παρ’ αὐτοῦ ἐπιστολὰς εἰς Δαμασκὸν πρὸς τὰς συναγωγάς, ὅπως ἐάν τινας εὕρῃ τῆς ὁδοῦ ὄντας, ἄνδρας τε καὶ γυναῖκας, δεδεμένους ἀγάγῃ εἰς Ἰερουσαλήμ.

records.literal_gloss: The but Saul still breathing threat and murder toward the disciples of the Lord, having gone to the high priest \v 2 asked from him letters to Damascus to the synagogues, so that if any he found of the Way being, men both and women, having been bound he might bring [them] to Jerusalem.

en.L: But Saul, still breathing threat and murder against the disciples of the Lord, went to the high priest \v 2 [and] asked from him letters to Damascus, to the synagogues, so that if he found any who were of the Way, both men and women, he might bring [them] bound to Jerusalem.
en.B: Saul, however, still breathed threats and murder against the Lord's disciples. Going to the high priest, \v 2 he requested letters to the synagogues of Damascus. With them he could put in chains any people of the Way he found there, men and women alike, and take them back to Jerusalem.
en.R: All this time Saul kept threatening to kill the Lord's followers. He went to the high priest. \v 2 He asked him for letters to the synagogues in the city of Damascus. Saul wanted to find people there who belonged to the Way, as the followers of Jesus were called. He wanted to arrest them, both men and women, and bring them back to Jerusalem as prisoners.

es.L: Pero Saulo, todavía exhalando amenaza y asesinato contra los discípulos del Señor, habiéndose presentado ante el sumo sacerdote, \v 2 le pidió cartas para Damasco, para las sinagogas, a fin de que, si encontraba a algunos que fueran del Camino, tanto hombres como mujeres, los llevara atados a Jerusalén.
es.B: Saulo, por su parte, seguía respirando amenazas y deseos de matar contra los discípulos del Señor. Fue a ver al sumo sacerdote \v 2 y le pidió cartas para las sinagogas de Damasco. Con ellas podría encadenar a cualquier persona del Camino que encontrara allí, hombres y mujeres por igual, y llevarla de vuelta a Jerusalén.
es.R: Durante todo ese tiempo, Saulo seguía amenazando con matar a los discípulos del Señor. Fue a ver al sumo sacerdote. \v 2 Le pidió cartas para las sinagogas de la ciudad de Damasco. Saulo quería encontrar allí a personas que pertenecían al Camino, como se llamaba a los discípulos de Jesús. Quería arrestarlos, tanto a hombres como a mujeres, y llevarlos presos de vuelta a Jerusalén.

sw.L: Lakini Sauli, akiwa bado anapumua vitisho na mauaji dhidi ya wanafunzi wa Bwana, alimwendea kuhani mkuu \v 2 [na] akaomba kutoka kwake barua kwa ajili ya Dameski, kwa masinagogi, ili kama angewakuta watu wowote walio wa Njia, wanaume kwa wanawake, awalete Yerusalemu wakiwa wamefungwa.
sw.B: Wakati huo Sauli bado alikuwa akipumua vitisho na mauaji dhidi ya wanafunzi wa Bwana. Alimwendea kuhani mkuu, \v 2 akaomba apewe barua kwa masinagogi ya Dameski. Kwa barua hizo angeweza kuwatia minyororoni watu wowote wa Njia ambao angewakuta huko, wanaume kwa wanawake, na kuwarudisha Yerusalemu.
sw.R: Muda wote huo Sauli aliendelea kutishia kuwaua wanafunzi wa Bwana. Alikwenda kwa kuhani mkuu. \v 2 Akamwomba barua za kupeleka kwenye masinagogi katika mji wa Dameski. Sauli alitaka kuwatafuta huko watu wa Njia, kama wanafunzi wa Yesu walivyoitwa. Alitaka kuwakamata, wanaume kwa wanawake, na kuwaleta Yerusalemu wakiwa wafungwa.

decisions.choice: but Saul, still: the story returns to Saul from 8:3
alternatives: a new episode with no link
decisions.reason: Saul was last seen ravaging the church in Jerusalem (8:1-3). Luke has followed Philip in between; "still" picks Saul up where he was left.

decisions.choice: breathing threat and murder: his whole being was set on threatening and killing the disciples
decisions.reason: Breath stands for what fills a person. Paul later says he persecuted the Way to the death and cast his vote against believers when they were put to death (22:4, 26:10).

decisions.choice: letters to the synagogues: the high priest's request that the Jewish communities of Damascus hand believers over
decisions.reason: The high priest had no power over the city of Damascus, in Syria, about 135 miles north-east of Jerusalem in a straight line. His letters asked the synagogues there to cooperate (22:5, 26:12).

decisions.choice: the Way: a name for the movement of those who follow Jesus
alternatives: a way of life in general
decisions.reason: Acts uses the word as a name for the believers and their teaching (19:9, 19:23, 22:4, 24:14, 24:22). It may echo "the way of the Lord" in Isaiah 40:3, which Luke 3:4 quotes of John the Baptizer.

decisions.choice: who belonged to the Way, as the followers of Jesus were called
decisions.reason: Readable explains the name, as the meaning note does.

decisions.choice: the purpose clause as a separate sentence
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable break the Greek sentence; the meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: el Camino, with a capital
decisions.reason: A name for the movement of those who follow Jesus (meaning decision m4); the capital shows it is a name, as in the English, and keeps it apart from the road of 9:17 and 9:27.

decisions.choice: discípulos at every level
decisions.reason: As the term sheet for this whole job settles, Spanish keeps "discípulos" even where the English Readable says "followers"; it is a plain word in Spanish. This holds for the whole chapter.

decisions.choice: Njia, with a capital
decisions.reason: A name for the movement of those who follow Jesus (meaning decision m4); the capital shows it is a name, as in the English, and keeps it apart from the road of 9:17 and 9:27.

decisions.choice: wanafunzi at every level
decisions.reason: As the term sheet for this whole job settles, Swahili keeps "wanafunzi" even where the English Readable says "followers"; it is a plain word in Swahili. This holds for the whole chapter.

source.text: ἐν δὲ τῷ πορεύεσθαι ἐγένετο αὐτὸν ἐγγίζειν τῇ Δαμασκῷ, ἐξαίφνης τε αὐτὸν περιήστραψεν φῶς ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ, καὶ πεσὼν ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν ἤκουσεν φωνὴν λέγουσαν αὐτῷ Σαοὺλ Σαούλ, τί με διώκεις;

records.literal_gloss: In now the proceeding it came to pass him to draw near to Damascus, suddenly and him flashed around a light from heaven, \v 4 and having fallen on the ground he heard a voice saying to him, Saul, Saul, why me do you persecute?

en.L: Now as he was going, it happened that he drew near to Damascus, and suddenly a light from heaven flashed around him, \v 4 and falling on the ground he heard a voice saying to him, "Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}?"
en.B: On his way, as he was nearing Damascus, all at once a light from heaven blazed around him. \v 4 He dropped to the ground and heard a voice speaking to him: "Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}?"
en.R: Saul traveled on and came close to Damascus. Suddenly a bright light from heaven shone all around him. \v 4 He fell down to the ground. Then he heard a voice. It said to him, "Saul, Saul, why are you attacking {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}?"

es.L: Y mientras avanzaba, sucedió que se acercaba a Damasco, y de repente relampagueó en torno a él una luz del cielo, \v 4 y, cayendo sobre la tierra, oyó una voz que le decía: «Saulo, Saulo, ¿por qué {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} persigues?».
es.B: Ya en camino, cuando se acercaba a Damasco, de pronto una luz del cielo resplandeció a su alrededor. \v 4 Cayó al suelo y oyó una voz que le decía: «Saulo, Saulo, ¿por qué {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} persigues?».
es.R: Saulo siguió su viaje y llegó cerca de Damasco. De repente, una luz muy fuerte del cielo brilló a su alrededor. \v 4 Saulo cayó al suelo. Entonces oyó una voz que le decía: «Saulo, Saulo, ¿por qué {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} atacas?».

sw.L: Basi katika kwenda kwake, ikatokea kwamba alikaribia Dameski, na ghafla nuru kutoka mbinguni ikamulika kumzunguka, \v 4 naye akianguka chini, akasikia sauti iliyomwambia, "Sauli, Sauli, kwa nini unanitesa?"
sw.B: Alipokuwa njiani akikaribia Dameski, ghafla nuru kutoka mbinguni ilimmulika pande zote kama radi. \v 4 Akaanguka chini, akasikia sauti ikisema naye, "Sauli, Sauli, kwa nini unanitesa?"
sw.R: Sauli aliendelea na safari, akakaribia Dameski. Ghafla nuru kali kutoka mbinguni ikaangaza pande zote kumzunguka. \v 4 Akaanguka chini. Kisha akasikia sauti. Ilimwambia, "Sauli, Sauli, kwa nini unanishambulia?"

decisions.choice: flashed around: shone around him like lightning
decisions.reason: The verb is used of lightning. Paul's own accounts say it was a great light at about noon, brighter than the sun (22:6, 26:13).

decisions.choice: Saul, Saul: his name in its Hebrew form, called twice
alternatives: the Greek form of the name
decisions.reason: Luke's narrative uses the Greek form of the name; the voice uses the Hebrew form, and 26:14 says it spoke in the Hebrew language. God calls a name twice in Genesis 22:11, 46:2, Exodus 3:4 and 1 Samuel 3:10.

decisions.choice: persecuting me: to persecute the disciples is to persecute Jesus himself
decisions.reason: Saul was attacking the believers, yet the voice asks why he persecutes "me". Jesus counts what is done to his followers as done to him (Luke 10:16).

decisions.choice: attacking
decisions.reason: Readable uses a common word for hunting down and harming people.

decisions.choice: Saulo, also in the call from heaven
decisions.reason: Spanish has two forms of the name: "Saúl", the Hebrew form and the name of the king, and "Saulo", the usual Spanish name of the apostle. The voice uses the Hebrew form (meaning decision m2), but the English keeps one name for the man throughout, so Spanish keeps "Saulo" and the reader is not led to think of two people.

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} on the free clitic
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks of himself, so the free pronoun "me" takes the deity_pronoun setting, as the English "me" does; clitics joined to the verb ("seguirlo") take none. This applies through the chapter.

decisions.choice: kutesa (L, B); kushambulia (R)
decisions.reason: In today's Swahili "kuudhi" mostly means to annoy or offend; "kutesa" is to persecute or torment, which is what Saul was doing to the disciples and so to Jesus (meaning decision m3). Readable says "kushambulia" (attack), as the English Readable does.

source.text: εἶπεν δέ· Τίς εἶ, κύριε;

records.literal_gloss: He said then, Who are you, Lord?

en.L: And he said, "Who are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, Lord?"
en.B: "Who are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, Lord?" he asked.
en.R: Saul asked, "Who are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, Lord?"

es.L: Y él dijo: «¿Quién eres, Señor?».
es.B: «¿Quién eres, Señor?», preguntó.
es.R: Saulo preguntó: «¿Quién eres, Señor?».

sw.L: Naye akasema, "Wewe ni nani, Bwana?"
sw.B: Akauliza, "Bwana, {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} ni nani?"
sw.R: Sauli akauliza, "Bwana, {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} ni nani?"

decisions.choice: Lord: a title of respect to a heavenly speaker, which the answer fills with its full sense
decisions.reason: The word can be a polite "sir" (16:30). Saul does not yet know who is speaking, but a light from heaven and a voice tell him he is facing a heavenly power. The answer, "I am Jesus", gives the word its full meaning.

decisions.choice: the deity pronoun setting on "you"
alternatives: no span, because Saul does not yet know who speaks
decisions.reason: The one addressed is the risen Jesus, so the pronoun takes the setting, as it does wherever Jesus is spoken to in Acts.

decisions.choice: ¿Quién eres?, no span
decisions.reason: Spanish needs no pronoun here, and adding "tú" would make the question sound challenging, so there is no free pronoun to carry the deity_pronoun setting that the English "you" has.

decisions.choice: Bwana, with a capital
decisions.reason: Swahili has one word for "sir" and "Lord", told apart only by the capital. Saul speaks to a voice from heaven, and the answer fills the title with its full sense (meaning decision m1, uncertain), so Swahili writes "Bwana" as the English writes "Lord".

decisions.choice: spans only on free pronouns and possessives
alternatives: a span on every pronoun the English marks
decisions.reason: As in John and Romans: Swahili marks most pronouns inside the verb ("unanitesa", you persecute me), and a prefix cannot take a capital, so the deity_pronoun setting applies only to free pronouns such as "wewe" and to possessives, and Swahili has fewer spans than English. At Literal "Wewe" opens the question and is written with its capital.

source.text: ὁ δέ· Ἐγώ εἰμι Ἰησοῦς ὃν σὺ διώκεις·

records.literal_gloss: The and [said], I am Jesus whom you persecute;

en.L: And he [said], "I am Jesus, whom you are persecuting.
en.B: He answered, "I am Jesus, and you are persecuting {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.R: The voice answered, "I am Jesus. You are attacking {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

es.L: Y él [dijo]: «Yo soy Jesús, a quien tú persigues.
es.B: Él respondió: «Yo soy Jesús, y tú {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} persigues.
es.R: La voz respondió: «Yo soy Jesús. Tú {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} estás atacando.

sw.L: Naye [akasema], "Mimi ni Yesu, ambaye wewe unamtesa.
sw.B: Akajibu, "Mimi ni Yesu, nawe unanitesa.
sw.R: Ile sauti ikajibu, "Mimi ni Yesu. Wewe unanishambulia.

decisions.choice: and he: the speaker answers; the verb of saying is understood
decisions.reason: The Greek has only "and he"; the reply follows at once.

decisions.choice: I am Jesus: the one Saul persecutes is alive, speaking from heaven
alternatives: a vision with no real presence
decisions.reason: Saul thought Jesus was a dead man and his followers deceived. Paul later counts this as the risen Lord appearing to him (1 Corinthians 9:1, 15:8), and Ananias and Barnabas say he saw the Lord (9:17, 9:27).

decisions.choice: SBLGNT: Jesus's words go straight on to "But get up" (9:6)
alternatives: the King James Version adds "it is hard for you to kick against the goads" and Saul's trembling question "Lord, what do you want me to do?"
decisions.reason: These added words have very little support in Greek manuscripts at this point. They appear in Latin witnesses and in the Greek text printed in the 1500s, and seem to have come from Paul's later accounts, where they belong: the goads in 26:14, the question in 22:10. Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: the voice
decisions.reason: Readable names the speaker as Saul heard him.

decisions.choice: and you are persecuting me
decisions.reason: Balanced makes the relative clause a plain statement, as Jesus's charge to Saul.

source.text: ἀλλὰ ἀνάστηθι καὶ εἴσελθε εἰς τὴν πόλιν, καὶ λαληθήσεταί σοι ὅ τί σε δεῖ ποιεῖν.

records.literal_gloss: But rise up and enter into the city, and it will be told you what you it is necessary to do.

en.L: But rise up and enter into the city, and it will be told you what you must do."
en.B: But get up and go into the city. There you will be told what you have to do."
en.R: But get up and go into the city. Someone there will tell you what you must do."

es.L: Pero levántate y entra a la ciudad, y te será dicho qué es necesario que hagas».
es.B: Pero ponte de pie y entra en la ciudad. Allí te dirán lo que tienes que hacer».
es.R: Pero levántate y ve a la ciudad. Allí alguien te dirá lo que debes hacer».

sw.L: Lakini inuka na uingie ndani ya mji, na itanenwa kwako lile ambalo ni lazima ulifanye."
sw.B: Lakini inuka uende mjini. Huko utaelezwa unachopaswa kufanya."
sw.R: Lakini inuka uende mjini. Mtu fulani huko atakuambia unachotakiwa kufanya."

decisions.choice: it will be told you: by someone not yet named
decisions.reason: The passive leaves the speaker open. 9:10-17 shows that the Lord sends Ananias, and 22:10-15 says Ananias told Saul what he was appointed to do.

decisions.choice: must: what God has purposed for Saul
decisions.reason: Luke often uses this word for what God has determined must happen (1:16, 3:21, 9:16).

decisions.choice: someone there will tell you
decisions.reason: Readable gives the passive a subject without naming who it will be.

source.text: οἱ δὲ ἄνδρες οἱ συνοδεύοντες αὐτῷ εἱστήκεισαν ἐνεοί, ἀκούοντες μὲν τῆς φωνῆς μηδένα δὲ θεωροῦντες.

records.literal_gloss: The and men the [ones] traveling with him stood speechless, hearing indeed the voice, no one however seeing.

en.L: And the men who were traveling with him stood speechless, hearing the voice but seeing no one.
en.B: The men on the road with him stood there unable to speak. They heard the voice, but they saw no one.
en.R: The men who were traveling with Saul stood there. They were too shocked to say anything. They heard the voice, but they could not see anyone.

es.L: Y los hombres que viajaban con él estaban de pie sin habla, oyendo, sí, la voz, pero sin contemplar a nadie.
es.B: Los hombres que iban de camino con él se quedaron allí sin poder hablar. Oyeron la voz, pero no vieron a nadie.
es.R: Los hombres que viajaban con Saulo se quedaron allí de pie. Estaban tan asombrados que no podían decir nada. Oyeron la voz, pero no podían ver a nadie.

sw.L: Na wale wanaume waliosafiri naye walisimama wakiwa wamepigwa butwaa wasiweze kusema, wakiisikia ile sauti, lakini bila kumwona mtu yeyote.
sw.B: Wanaume waliokuwa njiani pamoja naye walisimama pale, wasiweze kusema neno. Waliisikia ile sauti, lakini hawakumwona mtu yeyote.
sw.R: Wale watu waliosafiri na Sauli walisimama pale. Walishtuka mno hata wasiweze kusema chochote. Walisikia sauti, lakini hawakuweza kumwona mtu yeyote.

decisions.choice: the voice: the same voice that spoke to Saul
decisions.reason: The word means voice or sound; with the article it points back to the voice of 9:4. In Paul's own account in 22:9 the men with him saw the light but did not hear the voice of the one speaking to him. This account says they heard the voice but saw no one. Each passage is translated as it stands. The two may describe different sides of the event, such as hearing a sound without understanding words, but neither text explains how they fit together.

decisions.choice: seeing no one: they saw no person
decisions.reason: Saul saw the Lord (9:17, 9:27); his companions saw no one. In 22:9 they do see the light.

decisions.choice: speechless: struck dumb with fear or wonder
decisions.reason: The word describes people unable to speak for shock. In 26:14 they all fell to the ground.

decisions.choice: too shocked to say anything
decisions.reason: Readable says why they could not speak.

source.text: ἠγέρθη δὲ Σαῦλος ἀπὸ τῆς γῆς, ἀνεῳγμένων δὲ τῶν ὀφθαλμῶν αὐτοῦ οὐδὲν ἔβλεπεν· χειραγωγοῦντες δὲ αὐτὸν εἰσήγαγον εἰς Δαμασκόν.

records.literal_gloss: Rose up then Saul from the ground, having been opened however the eyes of him nothing he saw; leading by the hand then him they brought [him] into Damascus.

en.L: Then Saul got up from the ground, and though his eyes were opened, he saw nothing; and leading him by the hand they brought [him] into Damascus.
en.B: Saul rose from the ground. His eyes were open, yet he saw nothing at all, and his companions had to lead him by the hand into Damascus.
en.R: Saul got up from the ground. His eyes were open, but he could not see anything. So the men took his hand and led him into the city of Damascus.

es.L: Y se levantó Saulo de la tierra, y con los ojos abiertos nada veía; y guiándolo de la mano, lo hicieron entrar en Damasco.
es.B: Saulo se levantó del suelo. Tenía los ojos abiertos, pero no veía absolutamente nada, y sus compañeros tuvieron que llevarlo de la mano hasta Damasco.
es.R: Saulo se levantó del suelo. Tenía los ojos abiertos, pero no podía ver nada. Así que los hombres lo tomaron de la mano y lo llevaron a la ciudad de Damasco.

sw.L: Basi Sauli aliinuka kutoka ardhini, na ingawa macho yake yalikuwa yamefunguka, hakuona chochote; nao wakimwongoza kwa mkono, wakamleta ndani ya Dameski.
sw.B: Sauli aliinuka kutoka chini. Macho yake yalikuwa wazi, lakini hakuona chochote kabisa, na wenzake ilibidi wamwongoze kwa mkono hadi Dameski.
sw.R: Sauli aliinuka kutoka chini. Macho yake yalikuwa wazi, lakini hakuweza kuona chochote. Kwa hiyo wale watu wakamshika mkono, wakamwongoza mpaka mji wa Dameski.

decisions.choice: his eyes were opened, yet he saw nothing: he was blind
decisions.reason: The contrast is between open eyes and no sight. Paul says in 22:11 that he could not see because of the brightness of the light.

decisions.choice: they: the men traveling with him
decisions.reason: The subject is not named; the men of 9:7 are the only others present.

decisions.choice: his companions; the men
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name who led him.

source.text: καὶ ἦν ἡμέρας τρεῖς μὴ βλέπων, καὶ οὐκ ἔφαγεν οὐδὲ ἔπιεν.

records.literal_gloss: And he was days three not seeing, and not he ate nor drank.

en.L: And he was three days without seeing, and he neither ate nor drank.
en.B: He was without sight for three days, and all that time he neither ate nor drank.
en.R: Saul stayed blind for three days. During that time he did not eat or drink.

es.L: Y estuvo tres días privado de la vista, y no comió ni tampoco bebió.
es.B: Estuvo sin vista durante tres días, y en todo ese tiempo no comió ni bebió nada.
es.R: Saulo siguió ciego durante tres días. En ese tiempo no comió ni bebió nada.

sw.L: Na kwa siku tatu alikuwa haoni, wala hakula wala hakunywa.
sw.B: Kwa siku tatu hakuweza kuona, na muda wote huo hakula wala hakunywa.
sw.R: Sauli alibaki kipofu kwa siku tatu. Wakati huo wote hakula wala hakunywa kitu.

decisions.choice: he neither ate nor drank: a fast
alternatives: he had no appetite from shock
decisions.reason: The text does not say why. Fasting went with prayer and turning to God, and 9:11 says Saul was praying (compare 13:2-3, 14:23), but shock may also be part of it.

decisions.choice: three days without seeing: his blindness lasted three days
alternatives: he only kept his eyes shut
decisions.reason: The phrase continues 9:8. His sight returns in 9:18.

source.text: Ἦν δέ τις μαθητὴς ἐν Δαμασκῷ ὀνόματι Ἁνανίας, καὶ εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτὸν ἐν ὁράματι ὁ κύριος· Ἁνανία.

records.literal_gloss: There was now a certain disciple in Damascus by name Ananias, and said to him in a vision the Lord, Ananias.

en.L: Now there was a certain disciple in Damascus named Ananias, and the Lord said to him in a vision, "Ananias."
en.B: Living in Damascus was a disciple by the name of Ananias. In a vision the Lord called him: "Ananias!"
en.R: There was a follower of Jesus in Damascus named Ananias. The Lord spoke to him in a vision. He said, "Ananias!"

es.L: Y había cierto discípulo en Damasco de nombre Ananías, y le dijo el Señor en una visión: «Ananías».
es.B: En Damasco vivía un discípulo que se llamaba Ananías. El Señor lo llamó en una visión: «¡Ananías!».
es.R: En Damasco había un discípulo de Jesús llamado Ananías. El Señor le habló en una visión. Le dijo: «¡Ananías!».

sw.L: Basi kulikuwa na mwanafunzi fulani katika Dameski kwa jina Anania, na Bwana alinena naye katika maono, "Anania."
sw.B: Katika Dameski aliishi mwanafunzi mmoja jina lake Anania. Bwana alimwita katika maono, "Anania!"
sw.R: Huko Dameski kulikuwa na mwanafunzi wa Yesu aitwaye Anania. Bwana alisema naye katika maono. Akamwita, "Anania!"

decisions.choice: Ananias: a common Jewish name; not the Ananias of 5:1
decisions.reason: Paul later describes him as a devout man by the standard of the law, well spoken of by all the Jews living in Damascus (22:12).

decisions.choice: the Lord: Jesus
decisions.reason: In 9:17 Ananias says that the Lord who sent him is Jesus, who appeared to Saul on the road.

decisions.choice: a vision: something God shows a person, here with words spoken
decisions.reason: Acts uses the word for what is seen and heard from God, awake or asleep (10:3, 16:9, 18:9).

decisions.choice: a follower of Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what a disciple is.

source.text: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν· Ἰδοὺ ἐγώ, κύριε.

records.literal_gloss: The and he said, Behold I, Lord.

en.L: And he said, "Here [am] I, Lord."
en.B: "I am here, Lord," he answered.
en.R: Ananias answered, "Yes, Lord. I am listening."

es.L: Y él dijo: «Aquí [estoy] yo, Señor».
es.B: «Aquí estoy, Señor», respondió.
es.R: Ananías respondió: «Sí, Señor. Te escucho».

sw.L: Naye akasema, "Tazama, mimi [hapa], Bwana."
sw.B: Akajibu, "Nipo hapa, Bwana."
sw.R: Anania akajibu, "Ndiyo, Bwana. Ninakusikiliza."

decisions.choice: here I am: the reply of a servant ready to listen and obey
alternatives: a statement of where he was
decisions.reason: The same reply is given to God by Abraham (Genesis 22:1) and Samuel (1 Samuel 3:4).

decisions.choice: here
decisions.reason: The word points to the speaker himself; "here" is how English says it without an archaic word.

decisions.choice: Yes, Lord. I am listening
decisions.reason: Readable says what the idiom means, as the meaning note explains.

source.text: ὁ δὲ κύριος πρὸς αὐτόν· Ἀναστὰς πορεύθητι ἐπὶ τὴν ῥύμην τὴν καλουμένην Εὐθεῖαν καὶ ζήτησον ἐν οἰκίᾳ Ἰούδα Σαῦλον ὀνόματι Ταρσέα, ἰδοὺ γὰρ προσεύχεται, καὶ εἶδεν ἄνδρα ἐν ὁράματι Ἁνανίαν ὀνόματι εἰσελθόντα καὶ ἐπιθέντα αὐτῷ χεῖρας ὅπως ἀναβλέψῃ.

records.literal_gloss: The and Lord to him, Having risen up go to the street the [one] being called Straight and seek in [the] house of Judas Saul by name, of Tarsus; behold for he is praying, \v 12 and he saw a man in a vision, Ananias by name, having come in and having put on him hands so that he might see again.

en.L: And the Lord [said] to him, "Get up [and] go to the street called Straight, and seek in [the] house of Judas [a man] named Saul, of Tarsus; for look, he is praying, \v 12 and he has seen in a vision a man named Ananias coming in and laying hands on him so that he may see again."
en.B: The Lord said to him, "Get up and go to the street called Straight. There, at the house of Judas, look for a man of Tarsus by the name of Saul. Even now he is praying, \v 12 and he has seen a vision in which a man named Ananias comes in and lays his hands on him so that he can see again."
en.R: The Lord said to him, "Get up and go to the street called Straight Street. Find the house of a man named Judas. Ask there for a man from the city of Tarsus. His name is Saul. He is praying right now. \v 12 In a vision he has seen a man named Ananias. He saw Ananias come in and put his hands on him so that he could see again."

es.L: Y el Señor [le dijo] a él: «Levántate [y] ve a la calle llamada Recta, y busca en [la] casa de Judas a [un hombre] de Tarso llamado Saulo; porque mira, está orando, \v 12 y ha visto en una visión a un hombre llamado Ananías que entraba y ponía las manos sobre él para que volviera a ver».
es.B: El Señor le dijo: «Levántate y ve a la calle llamada Recta. Allí, en la casa de Judas, pregunta por un hombre de Tarso que se llama Saulo. En este momento está orando, \v 12 y ha visto en una visión que un hombre llamado Ananías entra y pone las manos sobre él para que vuelva a ver».
es.R: El Señor le dijo: «Levántate y ve a la calle que llaman Calle Recta. Busca la casa de un hombre llamado Judas. Pregunta allí por un hombre de la ciudad de Tarso. Se llama Saulo. Ahora mismo está orando. \v 12 En una visión ha visto a un hombre llamado Ananías. Lo vio entrar y poner las manos sobre él para que pudiera ver otra vez».

sw.L: Naye Bwana [akasema] kwake, "Inuka uende kwenye mtaa unaoitwa Mnyoofu, na katika nyumba ya Yuda umtafute mtu wa Tarso aitwaye Sauli; kwa maana tazama, anaomba, \v 12 naye ameona katika maono mtu kwa jina Anania akija ndani na kuweka mikono juu yake ili apate kuona tena."
sw.B: Bwana akamwambia, "Inuka uende kwenye mtaa unaoitwa Mnyoofu. Huko, katika nyumba ya Yuda, umtafute mtu wa Tarso jina lake Sauli. Hata sasa anaomba, \v 12 naye ameona maono ambamo mtu aitwaye Anania anaingia na kuweka mikono juu yake ili aweze kuona tena."
sw.R: Bwana akamwambia, "Inuka uende kwenye mtaa unaoitwa Mtaa Mnyoofu. Tafuta nyumba ya mtu aitwaye Yuda. Ulizia hapo mtu kutoka mji wa Tarso. Jina lake ni Sauli. Anaomba sasa hivi. \v 12 Katika maono ameona mtu aitwaye Anania. Alimwona Anania akiingia na kuweka mikono juu yake ili aweze kuona tena."

decisions.choice: the street called Straight: a main street of Damascus
alternatives: a description of any straight road
decisions.reason: Roman Damascus had a long, straight main street running east to west through the city; a street on its line is still there in the old city.

decisions.choice: of Tarsus: from Tarsus, a leading city of Cilicia
decisions.reason: Paul calls himself a Jew of Tarsus in Cilicia, a citizen of no unimportant city (21:39, 22:3).

decisions.choice: for he is praying: why Ananias will find him ready
alternatives: a mere report of what Saul is doing
decisions.reason: The word "for" gives the reason: Saul is praying, and God has already prepared him to receive Ananias (9:12).

decisions.choice: laying hands on him: a sign of blessing, here for healing
decisions.reason: Jesus laid hands on the sick (Luke 4:40), and so does Paul (28:8). In 9:17 the Holy Spirit is also given.

decisions.choice: look
decisions.reason: The word calls for attention; "look" is modern English for it.

decisions.choice: short sentences, one step at a time
decisions.reason: Readable breaks up the directions and the vision.

decisions.choice: la calle llamada Recta
decisions.reason: The street's name means straight (meaning decision m1). "Derecha" also means the right-hand side today, so "Recta" says the sense plainly.

decisions.choice: mtaa unaoitwa Mnyoofu
decisions.reason: The street's name means straight (meaning decision m1), and Swahili translates it as the English does. "Mtaa" (street) rather than "njia", which in this chapter names the movement (9:2) and the road Saul travelled (9:17).

source.text: ἀπεκρίθη δὲ Ἁνανίας· Κύριε, ἤκουσα ἀπὸ πολλῶν περὶ τοῦ ἀνδρὸς τούτου, ὅσα κακὰ τοῖς ἁγίοις σου ἐποίησεν ἐν Ἰερουσαλήμ·

records.literal_gloss: Answered but Ananias, Lord, I have heard from many about the man this, how many evil things to the holy ones of you he did in Jerusalem;

en.L: But Ananias answered, "Lord, I have heard from many about this man, how much evil he has done to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} holy ones in Jerusalem;
en.B: But Ananias answered, "Lord, many have told me of this man, and of how much evil he did to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} holy people in Jerusalem.
en.R: But Ananias said, "Lord, many people have told me about this man. They say he did terrible things to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} holy people in Jerusalem.

es.L: Pero Ananías contestó: «Señor, he oído de parte de muchos sobre este hombre, cuánto mal hizo a {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} santos en Jerusalén;
es.B: Pero Ananías respondió: «Señor, muchos me han hablado de este hombre y de todo el mal que le hizo a {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} pueblo santo en Jerusalén.
es.R: Pero Ananías dijo: «Señor, mucha gente me ha hablado de este hombre. Dicen que le hizo cosas terribles a {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} pueblo en Jerusalén.

sw.L: Lakini Anania akajibu, "Bwana, nimesikia kutoka kwa wengi habari za mtu huyu, ni mabaya kiasi gani aliyowatendea watakatifu {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} huko Yerusalemu;
sw.B: Lakini Anania akajibu, "Bwana, watu wengi wameniambia habari za mtu huyu, na jinsi alivyowatendea mabaya mengi watu {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} watakatifu huko Yerusalemu.
sw.R: Lakini Anania akasema, "Bwana, watu wengi wameniambia habari za mtu huyu. Wanasema aliwatendea watu {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} mambo mabaya sana huko Yerusalemu.

decisions.choice: your holy ones: the people who belong to the Lord, set apart for him
decisions.reason: This is the first time Acts uses the word for the believers (also 9:32, 9:41, 26:10). In the Old Testament Israel is a holy people (Exodus 19:6). "Your" makes them the Lord Jesus's own people.

decisions.choice: but: Ananias objects
decisions.reason: Ananias answers with what he knows of Saul, as if the Lord might not know it.

decisions.choice: holy people
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "holy ones"; Balanced and Readable say "holy people", as the letters to the Romans, Ephesians and Philippians do in this translation.

decisions.choice: tus santos (L); tu pueblo santo (B); tu pueblo (R)
decisions.reason: As the term sheet for the holy ones (meaning decision m1): Literal keeps "santos", which many readers take to mean especially holy individuals; Balanced and Readable say who they are, the people who belong to the Lord. The same choice holds in 9:32 and 9:41.

decisions.choice: watakatifu wako (L); watu wako watakatifu (B); watu wako (R)
decisions.reason: As the term sheet for the holy ones (meaning decision m1): Literal keeps "watakatifu", which many readers take to mean especially holy individuals; Balanced and Readable say who they are, the people who belong to the Lord. The same choice holds in 9:32 and 9:41.

source.text: καὶ ὧδε ἔχει ἐξουσίαν παρὰ τῶν ἀρχιερέων δῆσαι πάντας τοὺς ἐπικαλουμένους τὸ ὄνομά σου.

records.literal_gloss: and here he has authority from the chief priests to bind all those calling on the name of you.

en.L: and here he has authority from the chief priests to bind all who call on {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name."
en.B: Now he is here, and the chief priests have given him power to put in chains all who call on {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name."
en.R: Now he has come here to Damascus. The leading priests have given him the right to arrest everyone who prays to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}."

es.L: y aquí posee autoridad de parte de los jefes de los sacerdotes para atar a todos los que invocan {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} nombre».
es.B: Y ahora está aquí, y los jefes de los sacerdotes le han dado poder para encadenar a todos los que invocan {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} nombre».
es.R: Ahora ha venido aquí, a Damasco. Los jefes de los sacerdotes le han dado el derecho de arrestar a todos los que oran a {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}».

sw.L: na hapa ana mamlaka kutoka kwa wakuu wa makuhani kuwafunga wote wanaoliitia jina {{deity_pronoun:lako|Lako}}."
sw.B: Na sasa yuko hapa, na wakuu wa makuhani wamempa mamlaka ya kuwatia minyororoni wote wanaoliitia jina {{deity_pronoun:lako|Lako}}."
sw.R: Sasa amekuja hapa Dameski. Wakuu wa makuhani wamempa ruhusa ya kumkamata kila mtu anayekuomba {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}}."

decisions.choice: those who call on your name: those who pray to Jesus as Lord and belong to him
alternatives: those who say his name aloud
decisions.reason: Joel 2:32, quoted in 2:21, speaks of calling on the name of the Lord. Here the name is Jesus's (9:21, 22:16; 1 Corinthians 1:2).

decisions.choice: the chief priests: the high priest and the leading priestly families
decisions.reason: As in 4:23. In 9:1 Saul went to the high priest; here the whole priestly leadership stands behind him.

decisions.choice: bind: arrest and take prisoner
decisions.reason: As in 9:2 and 9:21, binding means taking people as prisoners.

decisions.choice: everyone who prays to you
alternatives: all who call on your name
decisions.reason: Readable says what the idiom means, as the meaning note explains.

decisions.choice: wanaoliitia jina lako
decisions.reason: "Kulitaja jina" is only to mention a name; "kuliitia jina" is to call on it in prayer, which is what the phrase means (meaning decision m1).

source.text: εἶπεν δὲ πρὸς αὐτὸν ὁ κύριος· Πορεύου, ὅτι σκεῦος ἐκλογῆς ἐστίν μοι οὗτος τοῦ βαστάσαι τὸ ὄνομά μου ἐνώπιον ἐθνῶν τε καὶ βασιλέων υἱῶν τε Ἰσραήλ, ἐγὼ γὰρ ὑποδείξω αὐτῷ ὅσα δεῖ αὐτὸν ὑπὲρ τοῦ ὀνόματός μου παθεῖν.

records.literal_gloss: Said however to him the Lord, Go, for a vessel of choice is to me this [man] to carry the name of me before Gentiles and also kings, sons also of Israel; \v 16 I for will show to him how many things it is necessary him for the name of me to suffer.

en.L: But the Lord said to him, "Go, for this [man] is a chosen vessel to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, to carry {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name before Gentiles and kings and [the] sons of Israel; \v 16 for I will show him how much he must suffer for the sake of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name."
en.B: But the Lord told him, "Go, because I have chosen this man as a vessel to bear {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name before Gentiles and kings and the people of Israel. \v 16 I myself will show him how much he will have to suffer for the sake of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name."
en.R: But the Lord said to him, "Go! I have chosen this man to work for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. He will tell people about {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. He will speak to people who are not Jews, to kings, and to the people of Israel. \v 16 I will show him how much he must suffer for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."

es.L: Pero le dijo el Señor: «Ve, porque este es para {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} un vaso escogido, para llevar {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} nombre delante de [los] gentiles y [de] reyes y [de los] hijos de Israel; \v 16 porque yo le haré ver cuántas cosas tiene que sufrir por causa de {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} nombre».
es.B: Pero el Señor le dijo: «Ve, porque he escogido a este hombre como instrumento para llevar {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} nombre ante los gentiles y los reyes y ante el pueblo de Israel. \v 16 Yo mismo le mostraré cuánto tendrá que sufrir por causa de {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} nombre».
es.R: Pero el Señor le dijo: «¡Ve! He escogido a este hombre para que trabaje para {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}. Él le hablará de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} a la gente. Hablará a los que no son judíos, a reyes y al pueblo de Israel. \v 16 Yo le mostraré cuánto tendrá que sufrir por {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}».

sw.L: Lakini Bwana akamwambia, "Nenda, kwa kuwa huyu ni chombo {{deity_pronoun:changu|Changu}} kilichochaguliwa, ili alichukue jina {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}} mbele ya watu wa mataifa na wafalme na wana wa Israeli; \v 16 kwa maana {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} nitamwonyesha jinsi ambavyo ni lazima ateseke sana kwa ajili ya jina {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}}."
sw.B: Lakini Bwana akamwambia, "Nenda, kwa sababu nimemchagua mtu huyu awe chombo cha kulipeleka jina {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}} mbele ya watu wa mataifa, na wafalme, na watu wa Israeli. \v 16 Mimi {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}} nitamwonyesha jinsi atakavyolazimika kuteseka sana kwa ajili ya jina {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}}."
sw.R: Lakini Bwana akamwambia, "Nenda! Nimemchagua mtu huyu anifanyie kazi. Atawaambia watu habari {{deity_pronoun:zangu|Zangu}}. Atasema na watu wasio Wayahudi, na wafalme, na watu wa Israeli. \v 16 Nitamwonyesha jinsi atakavyolazimika kuteseka sana kwa ajili {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}."

decisions.choice: a chosen vessel: an instrument the Lord has picked for a task
decisions.reason: The word means a jar or a tool; "of choice" means chosen. Paul uses the picture of vessels in God's hand in Romans 9:21-23 and 2 Timothy 2:20-21.

decisions.choice: to carry my name: to make Jesus known and bear witness to him
alternatives: to bear the name of Christian
decisions.reason: Saul has been attacking those who call on the name (9:14); now he will carry it to others (9:20, 9:27-28).

decisions.choice: Gentiles, kings and Israel: those Saul will speak to
decisions.reason: Acts shows him speaking to Gentiles (13:46-48), to King Agrippa (26:1-29) and to his own people (13:16, 22:1).

decisions.choice: he must suffer: suffering is part of the calling
decisions.reason: "Must" is the word of God's purpose, as in 9:6. Paul later lists what he suffered (2 Corinthians 11:23-28), and tells believers that many troubles lie on the way into God's kingdom (14:22). The text does not call it punishment.

decisions.choice: the sons of Israel: the people of Israel
decisions.reason: The phrase is the usual Old Testament name for the whole nation.

decisions.choice: I have chosen this man
alternatives: this man is a chosen vessel to me
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable turn "of choice" into a verb with the Lord as subject, as the meaning note explains.

decisions.choice: to work for me; tell people about me; people who are not Jews
alternatives: a chosen vessel; to carry my name; Gentiles
decisions.reason: Readable says what the images and the word Gentiles mean.

decisions.choice: un vaso escogido (L); instrumento (B)
decisions.reason: The Greek word is a vessel or container, used of a person as an instrument for a task (meaning decision m1). Literal keeps the picture of the vessel; Balanced says what it means, as the English does.

decisions.choice: los gentiles (L, B); los que no son judíos (R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide choice for these people: "gentiles" at Literal and Balanced, and at Readable the English Readable's plain explanation.

decisions.choice: chombo changu kilichochaguliwa (L); chombo cha kulipeleka jina langu (B)
decisions.reason: The Greek word is a vessel or container, used of a person as an instrument for a task (meaning decision m1). Swahili "chombo" is both a vessel and a tool, so it keeps the picture and the sense together at Literal and Balanced.

decisions.choice: watu wa mataifa (L, B); watu wasio Wayahudi (R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide choice for these people: "watu wa mataifa" at Literal and Balanced, since "mataifa" alone is the nations, and at Readable the English Readable's plain explanation.

source.text: ἀπῆλθεν δὲ Ἁνανίας καὶ εἰσῆλθεν εἰς τὴν οἰκίαν, καὶ ἐπιθεὶς ἐπ’ αὐτὸν τὰς χεῖρας εἶπεν· Σαοὺλ ἀδελφέ, ὁ κύριος ἀπέσταλκέν με, Ἰησοῦς ὁ ὀφθείς σοι ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ ᾗ ἤρχου, ὅπως ἀναβλέψῃς καὶ πλησθῇς πνεύματος ἁγίου.

records.literal_gloss: Went away then Ananias and entered into the house, and having laid on him the hands he said, Saul brother, the Lord has sent me, Jesus the [one] having appeared to you on the road by which you were coming, so that you may see again and be filled with [the] Spirit Holy.

en.L: Then Ananias went away and entered into the house, and laying [his] hands on him he said, "Brother Saul, the Lord has sent me, Jesus, who appeared to you on the road by which you were coming, so that you may see again and be filled with [the] Holy Spirit."
en.B: So Ananias went off and entered the house. He put his hands on Saul and said, "Brother Saul, the Lord Jesus, who appeared to you on the road you traveled, has sent me so that your sight may come back and you may be filled with the Holy Spirit."
en.R: So Ananias went to the house. He put his hands on Saul and said, "Brother Saul, the Lord Jesus sent me. He is the one who showed {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} to you on the road as you were coming here. He sent me so that you can see again and be filled with the Holy Spirit."

es.L: Entonces Ananías se fue y entró en la casa, e imponiéndole las manos dijo: «Hermano Saulo, el Señor me ha enviado, Jesús, el que fue visto por ti en el camino por el que venías, para que vuelvas a ver y seas lleno del Espíritu Santo».
es.B: Ananías fue y entró en la casa. Puso las manos sobre Saulo y le dijo: «Hermano Saulo, el Señor Jesús, que se te mostró en el camino por el que viniste, me ha enviado para que recuperes la vista y quedes lleno del Espíritu Santo».
es.R: Entonces Ananías fue a la casa. Puso las manos sobre Saulo y le dijo: «Hermano Saulo, el Señor Jesús me envió. Él es el que se te mostró en el camino cuando venías hacia aquí. Me envió para que puedas ver otra vez y seas lleno del Espíritu Santo».

sw.L: Basi Anania alitoka, akaingia ndani ya nyumba, na baada ya kuweka mikono juu yake akasema, "Ndugu Sauli, Bwana amenituma, Yesu aliyeonekana kwako katika barabara uliyokuwa ukiijia, ili uone tena na ujazwe Roho Mtakatifu."
sw.B: Basi Anania alikwenda, akaingia ndani ya nyumba. Akaweka mikono yake juu ya Sauli, akasema, "Ndugu Sauli, Bwana Yesu, aliyekutokea barabarani ulipokuwa ukija, amenituma ili uweze kuona tena na ujazwe Roho Mtakatifu."
sw.R: Basi Anania alikwenda kwenye ile nyumba. Akaweka mikono yake juu ya Sauli, akasema, "Ndugu Sauli, Bwana Yesu amenituma. Yeye ndiye aliyejionyesha kwako barabarani ulipokuwa ukija huku. Amenituma ili uweze kuona tena na ujazwe Roho Mtakatifu."

decisions.choice: brother: a fellow believer, welcomed into the family of God's people
decisions.reason: Jews called one another brothers (2:29, 22:1), but Ananias has just learned that Saul is the Lord's chosen vessel; the word welcomes the former persecutor as one of the believers.

decisions.choice: the Lord ... Jesus: the name explains who the Lord is
decisions.reason: Ananias names the Lord who sent him as the Jesus Saul met on the road.

decisions.choice: appeared: was seen by you
decisions.reason: The same verb is used of the risen Jesus appearing (13:31; 1 Corinthians 15:5-8). Saul saw him (9:27, 26:16).

decisions.choice: filled with the Holy Spirit: as the first believers were
decisions.reason: The believers were filled with the Spirit in 2:4 and 4:31. Luke does not say exactly when Saul was filled; 9:18 tells of his sight and his baptism.

decisions.choice: the Lord Jesus ... has sent me
alternatives: the Lord has sent me, Jesus
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable bring the name next to the title; the meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: a separate sentence: he is the one who showed himself to you
decisions.reason: Readable breaks up Ananias's words.

decisions.choice: se te mostró, no span
decisions.reason: The English Readable marks "himself"; Spanish says it with the reflexive "se", which is not a free pronoun for Christ, so there is nothing for the deity_pronoun setting to capitalise ("te" here is Saul).

source.text: καὶ εὐθέως ἀπέπεσαν αὐτοῦ ἀπὸ τῶν ὀφθαλμῶν ὡς λεπίδες, ἀνέβλεψέν τε καὶ ἀναστὰς ἐβαπτίσθη, καὶ λαβὼν τροφὴν ἐνίσχυσεν.

records.literal_gloss: And immediately fell of him from the eyes [something] like scales, he saw again also, and having risen up he was baptized, \v 19 and having taken food he was strengthened.

en.L: And immediately [something] like scales fell from his eyes, and he saw again; and rising up he was baptized, \v 19 and taking food he was strengthened.
en.B: All at once what looked like scales fell away from his eyes, and he could see. He stood up and was baptized; \v 19 then he took food and grew strong again.
en.R: Right away, something like scales fell from Saul's eyes. He could see again. He got up and was baptized. \v 19 Then he ate some food and felt strong again.

es.L: Y enseguida cayeron de sus ojos [cosas] como escamas, y volvió a ver; y poniéndose en pie fue bautizado, \v 19 y tomando comida se fortaleció.
es.B: De pronto, algo parecido a escamas se le desprendió de los ojos, y pudo ver. Se puso de pie y fue bautizado; \v 19 luego comió y volvió a sentirse fuerte.
es.R: En ese mismo momento, algo como escamas cayó de los ojos de Saulo. Ya podía ver otra vez. Se levantó y fue bautizado. \v 19 Después comió algo y se sintió fuerte de nuevo.

sw.L: Na mara moja [vitu] kama magamba vilidondoka kutoka machoni pake, naye akaona tena; na baada ya kuinuka alibatizwa, \v 19 na baada ya kupokea chakula, alitiwa nguvu.
sw.B: Ghafla kitu kama magamba kilidondoka kutoka machoni pake, naye akaweza kuona. Akasimama, akabatizwa; \v 19 kisha akala chakula, nguvu zake zikarudi.
sw.R: Papo hapo kitu kama magamba kilidondoka kutoka machoni mwa Sauli. Akaweza kuona tena. Akainuka, akabatizwa. \v 19 Kisha akala chakula, akajisikia mwenye nguvu tena.

decisions.choice: like scales: something like flakes; Luke says what it was like
decisions.reason: The word is used of fish scales and of flakes. Luke gives a comparison and does not name a condition.

decisions.choice: saw again: his sight came back
decisions.reason: The same verb as in 9:12 and 9:17: what the Lord promised happens.

decisions.choice: rising up he was baptized: at once, before he ate
decisions.reason: In 22:16 Ananias tells him to get up and be baptized without delay.

decisions.choice: Saul's eyes
decisions.reason: Readable names Saul to keep the people clear.

source.text: Ἐγένετο δὲ μετὰ τῶν ἐν Δαμασκῷ μαθητῶν ἡμέρας τινὰς, καὶ εὐθέως ἐν ταῖς συναγωγαῖς ἐκήρυσσεν τὸν Ἰησοῦν ὅτι οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ θεοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: He was then with the in Damascus disciples days some, \v 20 and immediately in the synagogues he was proclaiming Jesus, that this one is the Son of God.

en.L: And he was with the disciples in Damascus [for] some days, \v 20 and immediately in the synagogues he began proclaiming Jesus, that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is the Son of God.
en.B: Saul stayed for some days with the disciples in Damascus. \v 20 Without delay he went into the synagogues and proclaimed Jesus, telling them that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is the Son of God.
en.R: Saul stayed with the followers of Jesus in Damascus for several days. \v 20 Right away he began to go to the synagogues. He told the people there about Jesus. He told them that Jesus is the Son of God.

es.L: Y estuvo con los discípulos [que estaban] en Damasco algunos días, \v 20 y enseguida en las sinagogas proclamaba a Jesús, que este es el Hijo de Dios.
es.B: Saulo se quedó algunos días con los discípulos de Damasco. \v 20 Sin perder tiempo fue a las sinagogas y proclamó a Jesús, diciendo que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} es el Hijo de Dios.
es.R: Saulo se quedó varios días con los discípulos de Jesús en Damasco. \v 20 Enseguida empezó a ir a las sinagogas. Allí le hablaba a la gente acerca de Jesús. Les decía que Jesús es el Hijo de Dios.

sw.L: Naye alikuwa pamoja na wanafunzi [waliokuwa] Dameski kwa siku kadhaa, \v 20 na mara moja katika masinagogi alikuwa akimtangaza Yesu, kwamba huyu ndiye Mwana wa Mungu.
sw.B: Sauli alikaa siku kadhaa pamoja na wanafunzi wa Dameski. \v 20 Bila kukawia aliingia katika masinagogi, akamtangaza Yesu, akisema kwamba {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} ndiye Mwana wa Mungu.
sw.R: Sauli alikaa na wanafunzi wa Yesu huko Dameski kwa siku kadhaa. \v 20 Mara moja akaanza kwenda kwenye masinagogi. Akawaeleza watu huko habari za Yesu. Akawaambia kwamba Yesu ni Mwana wa Mungu.

decisions.choice: the Son of God: Jesus's unique relation to God, and the promised King
decisions.reason: This is the only place Acts uses the title in these words; 13:33 applies Psalm 2:7 to Jesus. In Psalm 2:7 and 2 Samuel 7:14 the king of David's line is God's son, and Luke 1:32-35 calls Jesus Son of the Most High and Son of God. 9:22 sets beside it the claim that he is the Christ.

decisions.choice: SBLGNT: "Jesus"
decisions.reason: Later manuscripts, followed by the King James Version ("he preached Christ in the synagogues"), have "Christ" here; the earliest manuscripts have "Jesus". Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: was proclaiming: began and went on proclaiming
decisions.reason: The verb is in the imperfect, for something done again and again.

decisions.choice: Saul
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Saul at the start of the scene.

decisions.choice: Jesus is the Son of God
alternatives: that he is the Son of God
decisions.reason: Readable names Jesus instead of the pronoun.

decisions.choice: que este es, no span
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek "this one" as the demonstrative "este", which is not a personal pronoun and takes no setting; Balanced uses "él" with the span, as the English does.

source.text: ἐξίσταντο δὲ πάντες οἱ ἀκούοντες καὶ ἔλεγον· Οὐχ οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ πορθήσας ἐν Ἰερουσαλὴμ τοὺς ἐπικαλουμένους τὸ ὄνομα τοῦτο, καὶ ὧδε εἰς τοῦτο ἐληλύθει ἵνα δεδεμένους αὐτοὺς ἀγάγῃ ἐπὶ τοὺς ἀρχιερεῖς;

records.literal_gloss: Were amazed then all those hearing and were saying, Not this is the [one] having ravaged in Jerusalem those calling on the name this, and here for this he had come, that having been bound them he might bring to the chief priests?

en.L: And all who heard were amazed and were saying, "Is this not the one who ravaged those in Jerusalem who call on this name, and had come here for this, that he might bring them bound to the chief priests?"
en.B: All who heard him were astonished. "Is this not the man who tried to destroy those in Jerusalem who call on this name?" they said. "Did he not come here for this very purpose, to take them in chains to the chief priests?"
en.R: Everyone who heard him was amazed. They said, "This is the man who tried to destroy the people in Jerusalem who pray to Jesus! He came here to arrest people like that and take them to the leading priests."

es.L: Y se asombraban todos los que [lo] oían, y decían: «¿No es este el que devastó en Jerusalén a los que invocan este nombre, y que había venido aquí con este fin, para llevarlos atados ante los jefes de los sacerdotes?».
es.B: Todos los que lo oían quedaban asombrados. «¿No es este el hombre que intentaba destruir en Jerusalén a los que invocan este nombre?», decían. «¿No vino aquí precisamente para eso, para llevarlos encadenados ante los jefes de los sacerdotes?».
es.R: Todos los que lo oían estaban asombrados. Decían: «¡Este es el hombre que trató de acabar con los que oran a Jesús en Jerusalén! Vino aquí para arrestar a esa gente y llevarla ante los jefes de los sacerdotes».

sw.L: Basi wote waliokuwa wakisikia walistaajabu, wakawa wakisema, "Je, si huyu ndiye aliyewaangamiza huko Yerusalemu wale wanaoliitia jina hili, na alikuwa amekuja hapa kwa kusudi hili, ili awapeleke kwa wakuu wa makuhani wakiwa wamefungwa?"
sw.B: Wote waliomsikia walistaajabu. Wakasema, "Je, huyu si yule mtu aliyejaribu kuwaangamiza huko Yerusalemu wale wanaoliitia jina hili? Je, hakuja hapa kwa kusudi hilo hasa, ili awapeleke kwa wakuu wa makuhani wakiwa wamefungwa minyororo?"
sw.R: Kila mtu aliyemsikia alishangaa. Wakasema, "Huyu ndiye yule mtu aliyejaribu kuwaangamiza watu wanaomwomba Yesu huko Yerusalemu! Alikuja hapa ili awakamate watu kama hao na kuwapeleka kwa wakuu wa makuhani."

decisions.choice: ravaged: tried to destroy
decisions.reason: Paul uses the same verb of himself in Galatians 1:13 and 1:23: he tried to destroy the church.

decisions.choice: is this not: a question that expects the answer yes
decisions.reason: The hearers know who Saul is; they are amazed at the change.

decisions.choice: those who call on this name: the believers in Jesus
decisions.reason: As in 9:14, calling on the name of Jesus marks those who belong to him.

decisions.choice: had come here: that was his purpose in coming
alternatives: he has now come for this
decisions.reason: The pluperfect looks back to why he came; the hearers see that he no longer acts on it.

decisions.choice: two questions
decisions.reason: Balanced breaks the long question in two; both expect the answer yes.

decisions.choice: statements instead of a question
decisions.reason: Readable states what the question implies, and says whom they call on.

source.text: Σαῦλος δὲ μᾶλλον ἐνεδυναμοῦτο καὶ συνέχυννεν τοὺς Ἰουδαίους τοὺς κατοικοῦντας ἐν Δαμασκῷ, συμβιβάζων ὅτι οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ χριστός.

records.literal_gloss: Saul however more was being empowered and was confounding the Jews those dwelling in Damascus, proving that this is the Christ.

en.L: But Saul was being strengthened all the more and was confounding the Jews who lived in Damascus, proving that this [one] is the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}.
en.B: But Saul's power kept growing. He threw the Jews who lived in Damascus into confusion, demonstrating that Jesus is the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}.
en.R: But Saul spoke with more and more power. The Jews who lived in Damascus could not argue against him. He showed them clearly that Jesus is the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}.

es.L: Pero Saulo era fortalecido más y más, y desconcertaba a los judíos que vivían en Damasco, probando que este es el {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}}.
es.B: Pero el poder de Saulo seguía creciendo. Dejaba confundidos a los judíos que vivían en Damasco al demostrarles que Jesús es el {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}}.
es.R: Pero Saulo hablaba con más y más poder. Los judíos que vivían en Damasco no podían discutir con él. Les mostraba claramente que Jesús es el {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}}.

sw.L: Lakini Sauli aliendelea kuongezewa nguvu zaidi, na kuwavuruga Wayahudi walioishi Dameski, akionyesha kwa ushahidi kwamba huyu ndiye {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}.
sw.B: Lakini uwezo wa Sauli uliendelea kuongezeka. Aliwavuruga Wayahudi walioishi Dameski, akionyesha wazi kwamba Yesu ndiye {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}.
sw.R: Lakini Sauli alihubiri kwa nguvu zaidi na zaidi. Wayahudi walioishi Dameski hawakuweza kubishana naye. Aliwaonyesha wazi kwamba Yesu ndiye {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}.

decisions.choice: the Christ: a title, the Messiah, the anointed King God promised
decisions.reason: With the article and after "is", the word is a title, not a name: Saul argued that Jesus is the one Israel was waiting for, as in 17:3 and 18:5.

decisions.choice: proving: showing by putting the evidence together
decisions.reason: The verb means to bring together, and so to show by comparing. In 17:2-3 Paul does this from the Scriptures.

decisions.choice: was being strengthened: grew stronger in his speaking and conviction
decisions.reason: He had regained his bodily strength in 9:19; here the growth is in his preaching, as the rest of the sentence shows.

decisions.choice: confounding: leaving them confused and without an answer
decisions.reason: The verb means to throw into confusion (compare 2:6).

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the one meant.

decisions.choice: the Christ, with "the Messiah" as the alternative
decisions.reason: Here the word is a title, so it keeps the article.

decisions.choice: el {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}}
decisions.reason: Here Christ is a title with the article (meaning decision m1), and Spanish takes the article with both words, so the span covers only the noun.

source.text: Ὡς δὲ ἐπληροῦντο ἡμέραι ἱκαναί, συνεβουλεύσαντο οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι ἀνελεῖν αὐτόν·

records.literal_gloss: When now were being fulfilled days many, plotted together the Jews to kill him;

en.L: Now when many days had passed, the Jews plotted together to kill him;
en.B: After a good many days, the Jews made a plan to kill him.
en.R: Many days later, the Jews in Damascus who were against Saul made plans to kill him.

es.L: Y cuando se cumplían muchos días, los judíos se pusieron de acuerdo para matarlo;
es.B: Después de bastantes días, los judíos hicieron planes para matarlo.
es.R: Muchos días después, los judíos de Damasco que estaban en contra de Saulo hicieron planes para matarlo.

sw.L: Basi siku nyingi zilipokuwa zikikamilika, Wayahudi walipanga njama pamoja kumwua;
sw.B: Baada ya siku nyingi kupita, Wayahudi walipanga mpango wa kumwua.
sw.R: Siku nyingi baadaye, Wayahudi wa Dameski waliompinga Sauli walipanga kumwua.

decisions.choice: many days: a long time; Acts does not say how long
decisions.reason: Paul says that after his call he went away into Arabia, returned to Damascus, and only after three years went up to Jerusalem (Galatians 1:17-18). Acts does not mention Arabia; the two accounts are not told in the same detail.

decisions.choice: the Jews: Saul's Jewish opponents in Damascus
decisions.reason: Saul was a Jew, and so were the disciples there. The word here means those who rejected his preaching (9:22).

decisions.choice: the Jews in Damascus who were against Saul
decisions.reason: Readable says which Jews are meant, as the meaning note explains.

source.text: ἐγνώσθη δὲ τῷ Σαύλῳ ἡ ἐπιβουλὴ αὐτῶν.

records.literal_gloss: became known however to Saul the plot of them.

en.L: but their plot became known to Saul.
en.B: But Saul learned of their plot.
en.R: But Saul found out about their plan.

es.L: pero fue conocida por Saulo la conspiración de ellos.
es.B: Pero Saulo se enteró de su complot.
es.R: Pero Saulo descubrió su plan.

sw.L: lakini njama yao ikajulikana kwa Sauli.
sw.B: Lakini Sauli alipata habari za njama yao.
sw.R: Lakini Sauli aligundua mpango wao.

decisions.choice: became known: Saul was told of it; the text does not say by whom
decisions.reason: The passive leaves the source unnamed.

source.text: παρετηροῦντο δὲ καὶ τὰς πύλας ἡμέρας τε καὶ νυκτὸς ὅπως αὐτὸν ἀνέλωσιν·

records.literal_gloss: They were watching closely also the gates day both and night so that him they might kill;

en.L: And they were also watching the gates closely day and night so that they might kill him;
en.B: They were even guarding the gates around the clock, waiting for the chance to kill him.
en.R: They watched the city gates day and night. They wanted to catch Saul and kill him.

es.L: Y vigilaban de cerca incluso las puertas, de día y de noche, a fin de matarlo;
es.B: Hasta vigilaban las puertas a todas horas, esperando la oportunidad de matarlo.
es.R: Vigilaban las puertas de la ciudad de día y de noche. Querían atrapar a Saulo y matarlo.

sw.L: Na walikuwa wakiyalinda kwa makini hata malango mchana na usiku ili wamwue;
sw.B: Walikuwa wakiyalinda hata malango mchana na usiku, wakivizia nafasi ya kumwua.
sw.R: Walilinda malango ya mji mchana na usiku. Walitaka kumkamata Sauli na kumwua.

decisions.choice: the gates: the gates in the city wall, the only ways out
decisions.reason: Damascus was a walled city. Watching its gates would catch Saul if he tried to leave.

decisions.choice: who watched: Acts names the Jews; Paul's own account names the governor
decisions.reason: In 2 Corinthians 11:32-33 Paul says that in Damascus the governor under King Aretas guarded the city to arrest him, and that he was let down in a basket through a window in the wall. Acts says the Jews watched the gates. Neither text says how the two fit together.

decisions.choice: around the clock
decisions.reason: Balanced uses the English idiom for the Greek one.

source.text: λαβόντες δὲ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ νυκτὸς διὰ τοῦ τείχους καθῆκαν αὐτὸν χαλάσαντες ἐν σπυρίδι.

records.literal_gloss: having taken however the disciples of him by night through the wall they let down him, having lowered [him] in a basket.

en.L: But his disciples took him by night and let him down through the wall, lowering [him] in a basket.
en.B: One night, though, his disciples took him and got him out through the wall, letting him down in a basket.
en.R: But one night Saul's followers helped him escape. They put him in a large basket. Then they let the basket down from an opening in the city wall.

es.L: Pero sus discípulos lo tomaron de noche y lo hicieron bajar a través de la muralla, soltándolo en un cesto grande.
es.B: Pero una noche sus discípulos lo tomaron y lo sacaron por la muralla, bajándolo en un cesto grande.
es.R: Pero una noche los discípulos de Saulo lo ayudaron a escapar. Lo metieron en un cesto grande. Luego bajaron el cesto por una abertura en la muralla de la ciudad.

sw.L: Lakini wanafunzi wake, wakiwa wamemchukua usiku, walimpitisha kupitia ukuta, wakimshusha ndani ya kikapu kikubwa.
sw.B: Lakini usiku mmoja wanafunzi wake walimchukua, wakamtoa nje kupitia ukuta wa mji, wakimshusha ndani ya kikapu kikubwa.
sw.R: Lakini usiku mmoja wanafunzi wa Sauli walimsaidia kutoroka. Walimweka ndani ya kikapu kikubwa. Kisha wakakishusha kikapu hicho kupitia mwanya katika ukuta wa mji.

decisions.choice: SBLGNT: "his disciples"
alternatives: many manuscripts read "the disciples took him"
decisions.reason: The earliest manuscripts have "his disciples". Many later manuscripts, followed by the King James Version, have "the disciples took him", which avoids giving Saul disciples of his own so soon. Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: his disciples: people who had come to believe through Saul's preaching
alternatives: the believers of Damascus in general
decisions.reason: With the SBLGNT reading, these are people Saul had taught in Damascus. Luke elsewhere calls believers disciples of the Lord (9:1), so some take "his" loosely.

decisions.choice: through the wall: through an opening in it
decisions.reason: Paul says he was let down through a window in the wall (2 Corinthians 11:33). Houses were sometimes built into a city wall (Joshua 2:15).

decisions.choice: basket: a large basket of woven rope or reeds
decisions.reason: The same word is used of the large baskets of leftover food in Mark 8:8.

decisions.choice: from an opening in the city wall
decisions.reason: Readable says how it was done, as the meaning note explains.

decisions.choice: un cesto grande
decisions.reason: The book-wide word for this large basket of woven rope (meaning decision m4), kept apart from the smaller "canasta".

decisions.choice: kikapu kikubwa
decisions.reason: The book-wide word for this large basket of woven rope (meaning decision m4), kept apart from the smaller "kikapu".

source.text: Παραγενόμενος δὲ εἰς Ἰερουσαλὴμ ἐπείραζεν κολλᾶσθαι τοῖς μαθηταῖς· καὶ πάντες ἐφοβοῦντο αὐτόν, μὴ πιστεύοντες ὅτι ἐστὶν μαθητής.

records.literal_gloss: Having arrived then in Jerusalem he was trying to join the disciples; and all were afraid of him, not believing that he is a disciple.

en.L: And having arrived in Jerusalem he was trying to join the disciples; and they were all afraid of him, not believing that he was a disciple.
en.B: Once in Jerusalem, Saul made attempts to join the disciples, but every one of them feared him; they could not believe that he had become a disciple.
en.R: Saul came to Jerusalem. There he tried to join the group of Jesus's followers. But they were all afraid of him. They did not believe that he was really a follower of Jesus.

es.L: Y al llegar a Jerusalén, intentaba unirse a los discípulos; y todos lo temían, sin creer que fuera discípulo.
es.B: Ya en Jerusalén, Saulo intentaba una y otra vez unirse a los discípulos, pero todos le tenían miedo; no podían creer que se hubiera hecho discípulo.
es.R: Saulo llegó a Jerusalén. Allí trató de unirse al grupo de los discípulos de Jesús. Pero todos le tenían miedo. No creían que de verdad fuera un discípulo de Jesús.

sw.L: Na baada ya kuwasili Yerusalemu, alijaribu kuambatana na wanafunzi; lakini wote walikuwa na hofu juu yake, kwa kutoamini kwamba ni mwanafunzi.
sw.B: Sauli alipofika Yerusalemu, alijitahidi tena na tena kujiunga na wanafunzi, lakini wote walimwogopa; hawakuweza kuamini kwamba alikuwa amekuwa mwanafunzi.
sw.R: Sauli alikuja Yerusalemu. Huko akajaribu kujiunga na kundi la wanafunzi wa Yesu. Lakini wote walimwogopa. Hawakuamini kwamba kweli yeye alikuwa mwanafunzi wa Yesu.

decisions.choice: arrived in Jerusalem: Paul's first visit after his call
alternatives: his return a few days later
decisions.reason: Paul says he went up to Jerusalem after three years to visit Cephas and stayed fifteen days (Galatians 1:18). Acts does not give the time.

decisions.choice: was trying: he tried again and again
decisions.reason: The imperfect describes repeated attempts that did not succeed.

decisions.choice: join: attach oneself to a group, become one of them
decisions.reason: The verb means to cling to or join closely (5:13, 10:28).

decisions.choice: the group of Jesus's followers; a follower of Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what a disciple is.

source.text: Βαρναβᾶς δὲ ἐπιλαβόμενος αὐτὸν ἤγαγεν πρὸς τοὺς ἀποστόλους, καὶ διηγήσατο αὐτοῖς πῶς ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ εἶδεν τὸν κύριον καὶ ὅτι ἐλάλησεν αὐτῷ καὶ πῶς ἐν Δαμασκῷ ἐπαρρησιάσατο ἐν τῷ ὀνόματι τοῦ Ἰησοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: Barnabas however having taken hold of him brought [him] to the apostles and related to them how on the road he saw the Lord and that he spoke to him, and how in Damascus he spoke boldly in the name of Jesus.

en.L: But Barnabas took hold of him [and] brought [him] to the apostles, and he described to them how on the road he had seen the Lord, and that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had spoken to him, and how in Damascus he had spoken boldly in the name of Jesus.
en.B: Barnabas, however, took him in hand and brought him to the apostles. He explained to them that on the road Saul had seen the Lord, who had spoken to him, and that in Damascus Saul had spoken out without fear in the name of Jesus.
en.R: But Barnabas helped Saul. He took him to the apostles. He told them how Saul had seen the Lord on the road, and how the Lord had spoken to him. He also told them how Saul had spoken bravely about Jesus in Damascus.

es.L: Pero Bernabé, haciéndose cargo de él, [lo] condujo ante los apóstoles, y les relató cómo en el camino vio al Señor, y que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} le habló, y cómo en Damasco habló con franqueza en el nombre de Jesús.
es.B: Bernabé, en cambio, se hizo cargo de él y lo llevó a los apóstoles. Les explicó que en el camino Saulo había visto al Señor, quien le había hablado, y que en Damasco Saulo había hablado sin miedo en el nombre de Jesús.
es.R: Pero Bernabé ayudó a Saulo. Lo llevó a los apóstoles. Les contó que Saulo había visto al Señor en el camino, y que el Señor le había hablado. También les contó que Saulo había hablado con valentía acerca de Jesús en Damasco.

sw.L: Lakini Barnaba, akiwa amemshika, alimleta kwa mitume, akawasimulia jinsi njiani alivyomwona Bwana, na kwamba alinena naye, na jinsi katika Dameski alivyonena waziwazi kwa jina la Yesu.
sw.B: Lakini Barnaba alimsaidia, akampeleka kwa mitume. Akawaeleza kwamba Sauli alikuwa amemwona Bwana njiani, na Bwana alikuwa amesema naye, na kwamba huko Dameski Sauli alikuwa amesema bila woga kwa jina la Yesu.
sw.R: Lakini Barnaba alimsaidia Sauli. Akampeleka kwa mitume. Akawaeleza jinsi Sauli alivyomwona Bwana njiani, na jinsi Bwana alivyosema naye. Akawaeleza pia jinsi Sauli alivyosema kwa ujasiri habari za Yesu huko Dameski.

decisions.choice: Barnabas: the Levite from Cyprus whose name means son of encouragement
decisions.reason: He was introduced in 4:36-37. Here he lives up to his name.

decisions.choice: he described: Barnabas; he had seen: Saul; he had spoken to him: the Lord
decisions.reason: The Greek uses "he" for three people. Barnabas is the subject of the sentence, so he is most likely the one who tells the apostles.

decisions.choice: the apostles: Acts speaks of the apostles as a group
decisions.reason: Paul says that on this visit he saw none of the other apostles except Cephas and James the Lord's brother (Galatians 1:18-19). Acts does not say which apostles were there.

decisions.choice: spoke boldly: spoke openly and without fear
decisions.reason: The same word is used of the apostles' preaching (4:13, 4:29, 4:31).

decisions.choice: Saul; the Lord
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the persons, as the meaning note explains.

decisions.choice: spoken bravely about Jesus
alternatives: spoken boldly in the name of Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable says what speaking in his name meant here.

source.text: καὶ ἦν μετ’ αὐτῶν εἰσπορευόμενος καὶ ἐκπορευόμενος εἰς Ἰερουσαλήμ, παρρησιαζόμενος ἐν τῷ ὀνόματι τοῦ κυρίου, ἐλάλει τε καὶ συνεζήτει πρὸς τοὺς Ἑλληνιστάς· οἱ δὲ ἐπεχείρουν ἀνελεῖν αὐτόν.

records.literal_gloss: And he was with them coming in and going out in Jerusalem, speaking boldly in the name of the Lord, \v 29 he was speaking also and debating with the Hellenists; they however were trying to kill him.

en.L: And he was with them, coming in and going out in Jerusalem, speaking boldly in the name of the Lord, \v 29 and he was speaking and debating with the Hellenists; but they were attempting to kill him.
en.B: From then on Saul was with them, going in and out among them in Jerusalem and speaking openly in the name of the Lord. \v 29 He spoke with the Greek-speaking Jews and argued with them, but they began making attempts on his life.
en.R: So Saul stayed with the apostles and went everywhere with them in Jerusalem. He spoke bravely about the Lord Jesus. \v 29 He talked with the Jews who spoke Greek and argued with them. But they kept trying to kill him.

es.L: Y estaba con ellos, entrando y saliendo en Jerusalén, hablando con valentía en el nombre del Señor, \v 29 y hablaba y discutía con los helenistas; pero ellos intentaban matarlo.
es.B: Desde entonces Saulo estaba con ellos y se movía con libertad entre ellos en Jerusalén, hablando abiertamente en el nombre del Señor. \v 29 Hablaba con los judíos de habla griega y discutía con ellos, pero ellos empezaron a intentar quitarle la vida.
es.R: Así que Saulo se quedó con los apóstoles y andaba con ellos por todas partes en Jerusalén. Hablaba con valentía acerca del Señor Jesús. \v 29 Conversaba con los judíos que hablaban griego y discutía con ellos. Pero ellos seguían intentando matarlo.

sw.L: Naye alikuwa pamoja nao, akiingia na kutoka katika Yerusalemu, akinena waziwazi bila hofu katika jina la Bwana, \v 29 akanena pia na kujadiliana na Wahelenisti; lakini wao walikuwa wakijaribu kumwua.
sw.B: Tangu hapo Sauli alikuwa pamoja nao, akienda huku na huku kati yao huko Yerusalemu, akisema waziwazi kwa jina la Bwana. \v 29 Alizungumza na Wayahudi waliozungumza Kigiriki na kubishana nao, lakini wao wakaanza kutafuta njia ya kumwua.
sw.R: Basi Sauli alikaa na mitume, akaenda nao kila mahali huko Yerusalemu. Alisema kwa ujasiri habari za Bwana Yesu. \v 29 Alizungumza na Wayahudi waliozungumza Kigiriki, akabishana nao. Lakini wao waliendelea kujaribu kumwua.

decisions.choice: coming in and going out: living and moving among them freely
decisions.reason: The same phrase describes Jesus's life among his followers in 1:21.

decisions.choice: the Hellenists: Greek-speaking Jews, here those who did not believe
decisions.reason: In 6:1 the word is used of Greek-speaking Jewish believers. In 6:9 Greek-speaking Jews from abroad argued with Stephen; now Saul, who had approved of Stephen's death (8:1), meets the same opposition.

decisions.choice: the Lord: Jesus
decisions.reason: The verse repeats what 9:27 said of Damascus, where Saul spoke boldly in the name of Jesus.

decisions.choice: Greek-speaking Jews; the Jews who spoke Greek
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the name means, as the meaning note explains; Literal keeps it.

decisions.choice: the Lord Jesus; the apostles
decisions.reason: Readable names the persons meant.

decisions.choice: los helenistas (L)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the group's name; "los griegos" would suggest Gentiles, while these are Greek-speaking Jews (meaning decision m2), as Balanced and Readable say.

decisions.choice: Wahelenisti (L)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the group's name; "Wayunani" or "Wagiriki" would suggest Greeks who are not Jews, while these are Greek-speaking Jews (meaning decision m2), as Balanced and Readable say.

source.text: ἐπιγνόντες δὲ οἱ ἀδελφοὶ κατήγαγον αὐτὸν εἰς Καισάρειαν καὶ ἐξαπέστειλαν αὐτὸν εἰς Ταρσόν.

records.literal_gloss: Having learned [it] however the brothers brought down him to Caesarea and sent away him to Tarsus.

en.L: But when the {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}} learned [of it], they brought him down to Caesarea and sent him off to Tarsus.
en.B: When the {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}} came to know of it, they brought him down to Caesarea and sent him on his way to Tarsus.
en.R: The other believers found out about this. So they took Saul down to the city of Caesarea, on the coast. From there they sent him home to Tarsus.

es.L: Pero al enterarse [de ello], los hermanos lo hicieron bajar a Cesarea y lo despacharon a Tarso.
es.B: Cuando los hermanos lo supieron, lo llevaron abajo, a Cesarea, y lo despidieron rumbo a Tarso.
es.R: Los otros creyentes se enteraron de esto. Entonces llevaron a Saulo a la ciudad de Cesarea, en la costa. Desde allí lo enviaron a su casa, en Tarso.

sw.L: Lakini ndugu, walipotambua [hilo], walimteremsha mpaka Kaisaria, wakamtuma aende Tarso.
sw.B: Ndugu walipojua habari hiyo, walimteremsha mpaka Kaisaria, wakamsafirisha aende Tarso.
sw.R: Waumini wengine waligundua jambo hilo. Kwa hiyo wakamchukua Sauli mpaka mji wa Kaisaria, ulioko pwani. Kutoka huko wakamtuma arudi nyumbani Tarso.

decisions.choice: the brothers: the believers in Jerusalem, men and women
decisions.reason: "Brothers" is the common word for fellow believers in Acts (1:15, 6:3).

decisions.choice: brought him down to Caesarea: down from the hill country to the port on the coast
decisions.reason: Jerusalem stands high in the hills, so one goes down from it. Caesarea was the harbor city where the Roman governor lived (8:40, 23:23-33). From there Saul could sail home.

decisions.choice: Tarsus: Saul's home city in Cilicia
decisions.reason: Saul was from Tarsus (9:11). Paul says that he then went into the regions of Syria and Cilicia (Galatians 1:21). Barnabas finds him there in 11:25.

decisions.choice: brothers and sisters, with "brothers" as the alternative
decisions.reason: The word here means the believers as a whole, as the meaning note explains.

decisions.choice: the other believers; on the coast; home
decisions.reason: Readable says who the brothers were and what the places were to Saul.

decisions.choice: hermanos, no gender span
decisions.reason: Spanish "hermanos" already includes the sisters (meaning decision m1), so it stays plain where the English has a gender span, as in the rest of the New Testament.

decisions.choice: ndugu, no gender span
alternatives: ndugu wa kiume na wa kike
decisions.reason: "Ndugu" already means brothers and sisters (meaning decision m1), so Swahili needs no gender span where the English has one.

source.text: Ἡ μὲν οὖν ἐκκλησία καθ’ ὅλης τῆς Ἰουδαίας καὶ Γαλιλαίας καὶ Σαμαρείας εἶχεν εἰρήνην οἰκοδομουμένη, καὶ πορευομένη τῷ φόβῳ τοῦ κυρίου καὶ τῇ παρακλήσει τοῦ ἁγίου πνεύματος ἐπληθύνετο.

records.literal_gloss: The indeed then church throughout whole of Judea and Galilee and Samaria had peace, being built up, and going on in the fear of the Lord and in the comfort of the Holy Spirit it was multiplied.

en.L: So then the church throughout all Judea and Galilee and Samaria had peace, being built up; and going on in the fear of the Lord and in the comfort of the Holy Spirit, it was multiplied.
en.B: So it was that the church across all of Judea, Galilee and Samaria had peace. It was being built up and walked in the fear of the Lord, and with the Holy Spirit's encouragement its numbers kept growing.
en.R: After this, the church everywhere in Judea, Galilee and Samaria had a time of peace. The church grew stronger. Its people lived with deep respect for the Lord. The Holy Spirit encouraged them, and more and more people joined the church.

es.L: Así pues, la iglesia por toda Judea y Galilea y Samaria tenía paz, siendo edificada; y andando en el temor del Señor y en el consuelo del Espíritu Santo, se multiplicaba.
es.B: Así fue como la iglesia en toda Judea, Galilea y Samaria tuvo paz. Se iba consolidando y vivía en el temor del Señor, y con el aliento del Espíritu Santo crecía en número.
es.R: Después de esto, la iglesia en todas partes de Judea, Galilea y Samaria tuvo un tiempo de paz. La iglesia se hizo más fuerte. Sus miembros vivían con profundo respeto por el Señor. El Espíritu Santo los animaba, y cada vez más personas se unían a la iglesia.

sw.L: Basi kanisa kotekote katika Uyahudi wote na Galilaya na Samaria lilikuwa na amani, likijengwa; na kwa kuenenda katika hofu ya Bwana na katika faraja ya Roho Mtakatifu, lilikuwa likizidishwa.
sw.B: Hivyo kanisa katika Uyahudi wote, Galilaya na Samaria lilikuwa na amani. Lilikuwa likiimarishwa na kuishi kwa kumcha Bwana, na kwa kutiwa moyo na Roho Mtakatifu likaendelea kuongezeka idadi.
sw.R: Baada ya hapo, kanisa kila mahali katika Uyahudi, Galilaya na Samaria lilipata wakati wa amani. Kanisa likazidi kuwa na nguvu. Watu wake waliishi wakimheshimu Bwana sana. Roho Mtakatifu aliwatia moyo, na watu wengi zaidi na zaidi wakajiunga na kanisa.

decisions.choice: SBLGNT: "the church", singular
alternatives: many later manuscripts read "the churches", with plural verbs
decisions.reason: The earliest manuscripts have the singular. Many later manuscripts, followed by the King James Version ("then had the churches rest"), have the plural throughout the sentence, perhaps to match 15:41 and 16:5. Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: the church: the believers of three regions seen as one church
